audit.whatIsWrong: The chart sides were shifted one row out of step with their own explanations: win[0]/phases[0] said Akshan while whys[0] reads "Level 1 favors you"; win[1] said Skill while whys[1] reads "Akshan out-pokes you at level 2"; win[2] said Wukong while whys[2] reads "Level 3 stays his".
audit.why: The packet levelChart matches the whys text exactly — Wukong / Akshan / Akshan / Wukong / Akshan / Wukong / Wukong — and it is the mechanically correct read: Wukong wins level 1 before Avengerang matters, loses 2-3 to ranged poke plus Heroic Swing, takes 4-5 back on the E-in trade.
audit.corrected: Rows 0, 1 and 2 flipped in BOTH layers as matched pairs to Wukong / Akshan / Akshan.

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldowns anywhere: Avengerang, Heroic Swing and Comeuppance were all named without numbers, so the 'wait for his E cooldown' advice had nothing to count.
audit.why: Avengerang is 9/8/7/6/5s, Heroic Swing is 18/16.5/15/13.5/12s, Comeuppance is 100/85/70s. The 18s rank-1 Heroic Swing is the punishable window the whole entry is built around, and it deserves to be stated.
audit.corrected: 9s Avengerang into phases[1].why, 18s Heroic Swing into phases[2].why and spikes[1].text, 100s Comeuppance into spikes[1].text.

audit.whatIsWrong: Heroic Swing was described only as a 'dash + camera swing escape' — the two conditions that let you beat it were never stated.
audit.why: Riot's own text: he fires a grappling hook into terrain then swings around it, and he gets knocked off when colliding with champions or terrain. So the ability needs nearby terrain to exist at all, and standing in his swing path drops him out of it. That is the concrete counterplay to the escape the entry tells you to respect.
audit.corrected: dosFull[0].d now states the terrain requirement and the champion-collision knock-off.

audit.whatIsWrong: wants.you[1] and spikes[0].text tell you to 'use W clone to reset his passive stacks'.
audit.why: Dirty Fighting's text says every three hits from attacks and abilities deals bonus damage and shields him — it says nothing about whether hits on a Wukong clone count toward that counter, or whether the counter decays. That is not in the kit file and I could not verify it, so I left both strings untouched rather than assert either way.

edits.before: W clone bails out any misstep and baits his answer. Only take the trade when Akshan's Heroic Swing is down.
edits.after: Avengerang is 9s at rank 1 and his passive fires a second shot — at 2 he chips you free unless minions block it.

edits.before: Full kit online — your core pattern starts now. Keep the wave near your side so Akshan must walk into your engage range.
edits.after: Heroic Swing lands at 3 on an 18s cooldown — his range plus that escape owns the trade until you can bait the swing out.

edits.before: His dash + camera swing escape. Engage when it's down. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: Heroic Swing needs terrain to hook, and colliding with a champion knocks him off it — block his exit.

edits.before: His R Comeuppance charges execute damage and his E swing lets him kite your all-in, so bait the E before you commit Cyclone.
edits.after: Comeuppance is 100s at rank 1 and scales with your missing health; Heroic Swing is 18s — bait the swing out, then commit Cyclone.

notes: The win[] row and the whys[] row disagreed on three of seven stages here — the sides were offset by one against their own explanations. Fixed to the packet chart, which matches the prose. Left the 'W clone resets his passive stacks' claim alone in two places because the kit text does not establish it.
